column1: # How people actually type Tamil in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# Every line here is a word the Tamil phonetic rules get wrong, because Latin
# spelling does not carry the difference:
#  - A long vowel nobody doubles ("vendam" is வேண்டாம், "pesu" is பேசு,
#    "amma" is அம்மா), and the e/o length the rules cannot know.
#  - Which n, l, r: retroflex ண against alveolar ன ("panam" is பணம்,
#    "thanni" is தண்ணி), ள against ல ("aval" is அவள்), ற against ர
#    ("nooru" is நூறு), ழ written l ("tamil" is தமிழ்).
#  - Gemination a single letter hides ("eduthu" is எடுத்து, "pathu" பத்து).
#  - Spoken forms and chat spellings ("evlo" எவ்ளோ, "apram" அப்றம்,
# The rules already handle t/d ட, th/dh த, zh ழ, ndr ன்ற, intervocalic tr ற்ற,
# a doubled k/ch/t/p between vowels, the long final e/o, -en/-om verb endings,
# the plural -gal கள், and -anum ணும்; words those rules get right are not
# A hand-written draft of the commonest few hundred words; it wants a Tamil
# speaker's review. Colloquial (spoken Chennai/central) forms are spelt the way
# Tamil chats spell them in script (இருக்கு, பண்ணு, வேணும்).
# Format: spelling<TAB>tamil   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
